title: Hashes
subtitle: HSET, HGET, HMGET, and efficient object storage

content.text: Hashes store field-value pairs under a single key. They are memory-efficient for storing objects with many fields.

content.code:
# Store user object
HSET user:1 name "Alice" email "alice@ex.com" age 30

# Get one field
HGET user:1 name

# Get multiple fields
HMGET user:1 name email

# Get all fields
HGETALL user:1

# Increment a numeric field
HINCRBY user:1 loginCount 1

# Delete a field
HDEL user:1 age

content.text: Use hashes instead of one string per field when an object has many attributes — it uses less memory.

questions.question: What command retrieves all fields and values from a Redis hash?
questions.explanation: HGETALL returns all field-value pairs in a hash.

faq.q: How many fields can a Redis hash have?
faq.a: Up to 2^32-1 (over 4 billion) fields per hash.
